propositions: After commit 465d's module split, all search_issues call sites moved out of transport.py into _base.py and _issues.py, but the structural guard still scans only transport.py, making the predicate return zero offenders unconditionally.

The guard test_no_search_issues_call_relies_on_the_default_page_size passes unconditionally because it AST-scans an empty file (transport.py contains zero search_issues calls post-split), violating its own documented invariant that it catches uncapped pagination calls.
The guard must be widened to scan all modules in adapters/jira_datacenter/ and must assert a non-zero count of observed search_issues call sites to prevent the same rot if code moves again.
A teeth test must prove the widened predicate detects an uncapped search_issues call in a non-transport.py module, confirming the directory-level scan actually works.
An audit of other single-file AST structural guards in the test suite found four more guards vacuously rotted by the same mechanism (apply, llm, fetch, and usage-log subsystems).
